files.lesson.md: --- order: 10 unit: fractions node: AC9M7N04 n2 assumes: [AC9M4N01 n1, AC9M4N01 n2, AC9M5N04 n1] title: Fractions, decimals and percentages summary: "One amount, three ways to write it. A percentage is out of 100, so 3/4 = 75/100 = 75% = 0.75. Divide the top by the bottom for a decimal; put a percentage over 100 and simplify for a fraction." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } connection: discount-compare # data/connections/maths.yml hook: "A 25% discount, a quarter off, 0.25 of the price: the same saving, written three ways. Which is easiest depends on the job." app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8174 url: http://127.0.0.1:8174/index.html readySelector: "#sl-c" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: bars.yml#explain-pic, caption: "$\\tfrac{3}{4}$ of the bar and 75 of the 100 squares: $\\tfrac{3}{4} = \\tfrac{75}{100} = 0.75 = 75\\%$." } explainClip: query: { code: "@bars.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "One amount, three names" say: "One amount can be a fraction, a decimal or a percentage." clip: - caption: { text: "3/4 of the bar. How many of 100 squares is that?", say: "Three quarters of the bar. How many of a hundred squares?" } - wait: 500 - caption: { text: "75 of 100: 75/100 = 0.75 = 75%.", say: "Seventy five out of a hundred: nought point seven five, or seventy five percent." } - click: Make c bigger - click: Make c bigger - click: Make c bigger - click: Make c bigger - click: Make c bigger - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "3/4 = 75/100" } - wait: 1200 --- You've written one amount as different fractions. **Percent** means "out of 100", so a percentage is a fraction with 100 parts: $40\% = \tfrac{40}{100}$. A **decimal** shows tenths, hundredths and thousandths: $0.40$ is 40 hundredths. A hundred grid shows why all three match, so you can move between them. ## Predict: three quarters ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a percentage for 3/4 shows whether they treat the digits as the percentage (34%) or think in hundredths." check: type: predict q: "Which is the same amount as $\\tfrac{3}{4}$?" options: - "$75\\%$" - "$34\\%$" - "$0.34$" - "$3.4\\%$" actual: "75%. 3/4 = 75/100 (× 25 on the top and the bottom), and out of 100 is a percentage: 75%. As a decimal, 0.75." ``` How many of 100 squares is three quarters? ## Run: shade the grid ```step stage: run insight: "Shading the hundred grid to match 3/4 turns the fraction into hundredths, which is what a percentage and a two-place decimal both are." try: { playground: board, starter: "bars.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "The bar is $\\tfrac{3}{4}$. Shade the same amount of the hundred grid. Was your prediction right?", when: "e = 1" } ``` $c$ is the number of squares shaded, out of 100. ## Investigate: converting ```step stage: investigate insight: "Each conversion goes through a fraction over 100 or a division: fraction to decimal by dividing, decimal to percentage by × 100, percentage to fraction over 100 then simplified. Max's mistake reads the digits after the point as the percentage." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Write $\\tfrac{3}{8}$ as a decimal." answer: "0.375" form: decimal feedback: - ["0.38", "That is rounded. 3 ÷ 8 is exactly 0.375."] - ["3.8", "Divide the top by the bottom: 3 ÷ 8."] explain: "3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. As a percentage: 37.5%." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#max" text: "Max writes $0.5$ as a percentage. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 4 fault: logic misconception: decimal-percent-place explain: "Line 4: 0.5 is 5 tenths, which is 50 hundredths. Out of 100: 50%. Multiply a decimal by 100 for the percentage." - check: type: answer q: "Write $16\\%$ as a fraction in its simplest form." answer: "4/25" form: simplest feedback: - ["16/100", "That is right, but 16 and 100 share 4. Simplify."] - ["8/50", "8 and 50 still share 2."] explain: "16% = 16/100 = 4/25 (÷ 4)." ``` ### Three ways Here is how to move between the three. ```worked \tfrac{3}{4} = \tfrac{75}{100} = 75\% :: Fraction to percentage: make it out of 100 (× 25 on the top and the bottom). \tfrac{3}{8} = 3 \div 8 = 0.375 :: Fraction to decimal: divide the top by the bottom. 0.375 \times 100 = 37.5\% :: Decimal to percentage: multiply by 100. 16\% = \tfrac{16}{100} = \tfrac{4}{25} :: Percentage to fraction: put it over 100, then simplify. 45\% = 0.45 :: Percentage to decimal: divide by 100. ``` Try one: write $\tfrac{3}{8}$ as a decimal. ### Find the mistake Read Max's working. How many hundredths is 0.5? ### Percentage to fraction ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: fifths on the grid, each direction of conversion, then the edge case of a decimal that never ends." try: { playground: board, starter: "bars.yml#fifths", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "bars.yml#fifths" hint: "One fifth of 100 is 20." check: { type: board, text: "The bar is $\\tfrac{2}{5}$. Shade the same amount of the grid.", when: "e = 1", explain: "2/5 = 40/100 = 40%." } - check: type: answer q: "Write $0.6$ as a percentage (a number of percent)." answer: "60" feedback: - ["6", "0.6 is 6 tenths, which is 60 hundredths."] - ["0.6", "Multiply by 100 for the percentage."] explain: "0.6 × 100 = 60%." - check: type: answer q: "Write $35\\%$ as a decimal." answer: "0.35" form: decimal feedback: - ["3.5", "Divide by 100, not by 10."] - ["35", "35% is 35 out of 100: divide by 100."] explain: "35 ÷ 100 = 0.35." - check: type: answer q: "Write $\\tfrac{7}{20}$ as a percentage." answer: "35" feedback: - ["0.35", "That is the decimal. Multiply by 100 for the percent."] - ["720", "Make it out of 100: × 5 on the top and the bottom."] explain: "7/20 = 35/100 = 35%." - check: type: question q: "Edge case: what is $\\tfrac{1}{3}$ as a decimal?" options: ["0.333…, with the 3s going on for ever", "0.3 exactly", "0.33 exactly", "3.3"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "3 × 0.3 = 0.9, not 1.", "3 × 0.33 = 0.99, not 1.", "1 ÷ 3 is less than 1."] explain: "1 ÷ 3 = 0.333…: a recurring decimal. Still a rational number (a fraction); the grid shows about 33.3 squares." ``` ### Fifths Each task changes one thing. ### Decimal to percentage ### Percentage to decimal ### Fraction to percentage ### A decimal that never ends ## Practise: all three ```step stage: practise insight: "Conversions in every direction, mixed, with digit-reading planted again; ordering mixed forms; the review keeps simplifying fresh." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Write $0.45$ as a fraction in its simplest form." answer: "9/20" form: simplest feedback: - ["45/100", "Simplify: 45 and 100 share 5."] explain: "0.45 = 45/100 = 9/20." - check: type: answer q: "Write $\\tfrac{3}{5}$ as a percentage." answer: "60" feedback: - ["35", "3/5 is not 35%: make it out of 100 (× 20)."] - ["0.6", "That is the decimal. × 100 for the percent."] explain: "3/5 = 60/100 = 60%." - check: type: question q: "Which is smallest: $0.6$, $\\tfrac{2}{3}$ or $65\\%$?" options: ["0.6", "2/3", "65%"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "2/3 = 0.666…, which is more than 0.65.", "65% = 0.65, more than 0.6."] explain: "Write each as a decimal: 0.6, 0.666… and 0.65. The smallest is 0.6." - check: type: answer q: "Review: write $\\tfrac{9}{12}$ in its simplest form." answer: "3/4" form: simplest feedback: - ["9/12", "9 and 12 share 3."] explain: "÷ 3: 3/4." ``` ### Decimal to fraction ### Fraction to percentage ### Order them ### Review: simplest form ## Make: eighths that are whole percentages ```step stage: make insight: "Searching eighths for whole-number percentages shows which fractions fit hundredths exactly, and that the rest (3/8 = 37.5%) need a decimal." try: { playground: board, starter: "bars.yml#make", height: 600 } hint: ["1/8 = 12.5%: not a whole number.", "Try 2/8: simplify it first."] check: { type: board, text: "Choose a number of eighths ($a$) that is a whole-number percentage, then shade the same amount on the grid.", when: "e = 1 and a > 0", explain: "2/8 = 25%, 4/8 = 50%, 6/8 = 75% (and 8/8 = 100%). Odd numbers of eighths end in .5%." } ``` Which eighths cannot be shaded exactly on the grid? Why? ## Make: two sale signs on paper ```step stage: make insight: "Comparing a fraction off with a percentage off needs one form for both; the paper task makes them choose that form and say why." hint: ["Write 1/5 as a percentage.", "Work out each sale price: take the discount off \\$80."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Two shops sell the same \\$80 pair of boots (the prices are made up for the task). Shop A has a fifth off. Shop B has 25% off. What is the lower of the two sale prices, in dollars?" steps: - ["$\\tfrac{1}{5} = \\tfrac{20}{100} = 20\\%$", "multiply the top and the bottom by 20 to get hundredths"] - ["Shop B's 25% is bigger than Shop A's 20%", "once both are percentages, they can be compared"] - ["Shop B takes off 25% of \\$80, which is \\$20, so the price is \\$60", "a quarter of 80 is 20, and 80 − 20 = 60"] - ["Shop A takes off 20% of \\$80, which is \\$16, so the price is \\$64", "check: \\$64 is more than \\$60, as the percentages said"] picks: - step: 1 q: "Why write a fifth as a percentage before comparing?" options: - "Then both discounts are in the same form, and 20% and 25% can be compared" - "Because a fifth is always smaller than a percentage" - "Because percentages are more accurate than fractions" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A fifth is not always smaller. 1/5 is 20% and 25% is a quarter: it depends on the amounts.", "They are the same amount in different forms. The form only matters for comparing."] answer: "60" feedback: - ["64", "That is Shop A's price. Shop B's 25% off is more than a fifth off."] - ["20", "That is how much Shop B takes off, not the price. Take it off the \\$80."] criteria: - "I wrote both discounts in the same form before comparing them." - "I worked out both sale prices, not just one." - "My cheaper shop is the one with the bigger discount." explain: "A fifth is 20%, so Shop B's 25% is the bigger discount. 25% of 80 is 20, so the price is 60. Shop A's price is 64." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The prices are made up for the task, but the question is real: sale signs are written in different forms, and you have to put them in one form to compare. Write both as percentages, work out the prices, and type the lower one. **Also used in** - **Sales.** "A third off" and "30% off" sit next to each other in shop windows, and the third is the bigger discount. - **Sport.** A win rate of 7 out of 10 and 65% are compared by writing them the same way. - **Test marks.** 17 out of 20 and 82% are put on the same footing as percentages or as decimals. ```teacher summary: Students use a fraction bar and a hundred grid to see one amount as a fraction, a decimal and a percentage, convert in every direction, and meet a recurring decimal (AC9M7N04, node 2). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can convert between fractions, decimals and percentages. - I can explain why 0.5 = 50%, not 5%. - I can compare amounts written in different forms. struggle: Treating the digits as the percentage (0.5 as 5%, 3/4 as 34%). Ask "out of how many?" and point at the hundred grid before they write the percent sign. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need Equivalent fractions (the lesson before) and place value with decimals (Year 6). The one idea: percent means out of 100, so hundredths connect all three. The common mistake is reading the digits after the point as the percentage (0.5 = 5%); it is planted in Max's working and named in the success criteria. Decimal answers are marked by form (3/8 is told to write a decimal); a percentage can be typed with or without the % sign. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Students who chose 34% are reading digits." - "Run: ask how many squares one quarter is, then three." - "Investigate: model each line of the worked example with the grid beside it." - "Modify: before the 1/3 task, ask students to shade 1/3 of the grid exactly." - "Make: ask why odd numbers of eighths cannot be shaded exactly." - "Paper: the two sale signs are worked in books; the page marks the lower price (60) and why both discounts go into one form first. Books out, then look for the fifth written as 20% before any prices." stuck: - see: A student writes 0.5 as 5% (Max's mistake). ask: How many hundredths is 0.5? Shade it on the grid. fix: "× 100: 0.5 = 50%." - see: A student writes 3/4 as 3.4 or 0.34. ask: "What does the fraction bar mean: 3 of 4 parts. What is 3 ÷ 4?" fix: "Divide the top by the bottom: 0.75." - see: A student cannot simplify a percentage as a fraction. ask: What do 16 and 100 have in common? fix: Over 100, then divide by the highest common factor. stretch: Which fractions with a bottom number up to 12 give decimals that stop, and which recur? What do the stopping ones have in common? (In simplest form, bottoms made only of 2s and 5s.) support: Use the hundred grid for every conversion; for eighths, allow half squares. leads: > Next: Fractions and decimals on the line (node 3). Where it leads: percentage of an amount, percentage change and discounts (Year 8), and probability. exit: q: Write 3/5 as a decimal and as a percentage, and 0.08 as a percentage. a: 0.6 and 60%; 0.08 = 8%. explain: > **Percent** means out of 100, so a percentage is a fraction over 100: $75\% = \tfrac{75}{100} = \tfrac{3}{4}$. A decimal counts tenths and hundredths: $0.75$ is 75 hundredths. - Fraction to decimal: divide the top by the bottom ($\tfrac{3}{8} = 0.375$). - Decimal to percentage: × 100 ($0.5 = 50\%$, not 5%). - Percentage to fraction: over 100, then simplify ($16\% = \tfrac{4}{25}$). Some decimals never end: $\tfrac{1}{3} = 0.333\ldots$ ```
